aspect: The herder-farmer displacement, by the numbers
description: From January 2015 to February 2017 at least 62,000 people were displaced in Kaduna, Benue and Plateau - and with no IDP camps available most sheltered in other poor rural communities. An estimated 300,000 fled after the January 2018 escalation, and by 2025 close to 500,000 people in Benue had been displaced.
energy_note: Half a million people, in one state, with nowhere organised to go.

aspect: The scale of the conflict producing it
description: Violence has affected more than 20 states, particularly Benue, Plateau, Taraba, Adamawa, Kaduna, Kwara, Borno and Zamfara. In 2016 one count put herder-related deaths at 1,425 against 1,240 attributed to Boko Haram in the same period.
energy_note: Deadlier than the insurgency, in the year nobody reported it.

aspect: Hosting is unfunded and has a half-life
description: Displaced families absorbed by relatives strain households that were already poor. The first month is solidarity; by the third the food, space and goodwill are gone, and nobody can say so.
energy_note: A welcome you can feel expiring.

description: Farmland not worked for a season is farmland claimed, degraded or occupied. Displacement that is temporary in intention becomes permanent through the agricultural calendar.
energy_note: One missed planting season, and it is not yours.

aspect: Women's work is where the strain lands
description: Water, fuel, food and childcare in an unfamiliar place with no infrastructure are performed by women, and the hours are counted as leisure in every time-use survey.
time_note: Days per year of additional unpaid logistics.
energy_note: Four extra hours a day, uncounted.

energy_note: Half a million people, in one state, and no camps.
